(AI-generated image for representational purposes only) AI Quick Read The 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) may consider a range of changes to salaries, pensions, allowances, and service benefits of Central Government employees . The 8th Pay Commission was announced in January 2025 and formally constituted on 3 November 2025. It has been given 18 months to submit its recommendations. While the revised pay structure is expected to take effect from 1 January 2026, the government has clarified that the final implementation date will be decided separately. Against this backdrop, the Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh (BPMS), an all-India federation of defence workers recognised by the Ministry of Defence, submitted a fresh set of demands to the 8th CPC chairman on 18 November 2026 during its second-round interaction. The proposals highlight the expectations and concerns of Central Government employees, particularly Defence Civilian Employees. What are the key salary and pension demands? The BPMS has proposed several changes to the existing pay and pension structure, including: Minimum pay: Determine minimum pay using actual family consumption requirements, Indian Labour Conference norms and the Aykroyd formula, factoring in prevailing prices. Fitment factor: Recommend an appropriate fitment factor to offset inflation and protect purchasing power, maintain reasonable pay gaps between successive Pay Levels, and cap the maximum-to-minimum pay ratio at 1:10. Annual increment: Increase the existing annual increment from 3% to 6% of basic pay. DA merger: Merge 50% of existing dearness allowance (DA) with basic pay and pension before revising the pay structure. Old Pension Scheme (OPS): Discontinue NPS and UPS and restore the defined-benefit OPS for Central Government employees. Bonus: Extend ad-hoc and productivity-linked bonuses to all employees, including senior-level employees, with a minimum entitlement equivalent to 30 days' pay plus DA. Insurance: Increase Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEGIS) cover from ₹ 30,000 to at least ₹ 15 lakh and Deposit Linked Insurance benefits to ₹ 10 lakh. Other financial benefits: Ensure GPF interest is not lower than EPF interest and restore discontinued or restricted interest-free advances. The federation has proposed: Increase casual leave to 12 days annually. Allow 20 days' leave encashment on each eligible LTC occasion and reintroduce the LTC Special Cash Package. Increase paternity leave to 45 days, including adoption cases. Extend child care leave to two years with full wages. Allow re-employed ex-servicemen leave encashment up to 300 days without deducting encashment from previous military service. Introduce one day of menstrual leave monthly. Increase special casual leave for trade union activities to 60 days for office-bearers and 30 days for executive committee members. Provide work-related illness and injury leave (WRIL) with full leave salary, alongside compensation under the Employees' Compensation Act. Also Read | Pension, gratuity, GPF and more: What family gets after govt employee's death? What other service-related changes has BPMS proposed? The federation has sought a dynamic promotion system, replacing vacancy-based promotions, and at least five financial upgradations under Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) over 30 years. It also wants retrospective effect for delayed DPC recommendations, a maximum five-year residency period in feeder grades, common recruitment rules, rotation of Group C employees within the same station, and consultation with JCM representatives before identifying sensitive posts. Other demands include a centralised portal for compassionate inter-ministry transfers, equal pension revision for pre- and post-1 January 2026 retirees, fair pay fixation for re-employed ex-servicemen, pay protection during redeployment, parity in special allowances for civilian and uniformed personnel performing similar duties, and a stronger Joint Consultative Machinery (JCM). Disclaimer: The demands mentioned are proposals submitted by the employee union to the 8th Pay Commission and are not final recommendations or approved changes.
